meta.title: Gomsdu Glyphic System — working reference data
meta.purpose: Structured, machine-readable store of the Gomsdu Glyphic System's Glyphs, sounds, and meanings, plus its grammar rules. Intended as the data layer for a future sentence-composition interface, not just documentation.
meta.compiledFrom: Design conversation with Claude, cross-check against creator's notebook for accuracy
meta.renderingNote: Each primitive's 'render' field is an SVG-style path drawn in a local 0-100 x 0-100 box — a first-pass geometric interpretation for prototyping, not final art. Word 'composition' entries place primitives (or other words) using normalized position [x, y] (0-1 fraction of the glyph's own bounding box), scale (0-1 fraction of parent size), and rotation (degrees), so a renderer can compose them at any pixel size.
meta.status: living document — expect frequent additions as new words are coined
correctionLog: 2026-08-19 — First creator review after ~4 AI-drafted passes (the Codex was only given to the drafting Claude on the 2nd-to-last pass). Corrected: KROW/GOM chevron placement (apex now sits outside the container, not centered inside it), jagged-circle redesign (many-straight-segment circle with small Taurus-style horns — was reading as a spiky hexagon), KUL's arrowhead direction (was inverted, tips pointed inward instead of outward), KULKROW's nested KUL rescaled so its cross touches the container's boundary, BIS rebuilt from two chevrons instead of 'teepees', LANGUAGE rebuilt to flank WIM_MIW with BIS's two halves instead of fusing whole BIS beside it, GOMGOM's horn-overlap direction, and a viewer-wide switch from rounded to sharp/jagged line caps, joins, and corners. Also clarified as a grammar point: horizontal mirroring/reading order carries no grammatical meaning (BIS read backward as SIB is equally valid). 'Wimbis' floated as a candidate sound for the Language compound (WIM + BIS).

2026-08-19, later — Creator hand-edited this file directly and left it syntactically invalid (three trailing commas); fixed. Per creator's verbal clarification: BIS rebuilt again — it's 4 chevrons, not 2, forming two stacked diamonds (small 'v' above big 'V', same overlapping-pair construction as WIM, tips touching at the seam), not one nested v-in-V sharing an apex. LANGUAGE's dangling reference to the retired id 'WIM_MIW' fixed to 'WIM', and its flanking halves updated to match BIS's new shape. WIM's own notes corrected — word-order-sets-direction is a general rule, not unique to WIM; what's actually unique to WIM is that its meaning names a specific teacher-to-pupil relationship, a more advanced idea deferred past 1st Era Language. GO_KROW and SUU intentionally removed (GO_KROW was a Grammar-Line demonstration superseded by the Line composer; SUU isn't being written down yet) — not accidental. Sound for LANGUAGE settled as 'wimbis'.

2026-08-20 — Added new primitives 'dot' (a real filled circle, round on purpose — the one shape allowed to break the straight-lines-only rule) and 'compass' (the four-outer-position rhombus outline). Added five new words: GI (a Word/single Glyph), GeKA (a Diglyph), GeKARAP (a Triglyph), ZON (Self), and ZIN (I — Crystal Being secret translation: Heart). New 'meta' category introduced for GI/GeKA/GeKARAP. Corrected same day: ZIN's meaning was backward (public meaning is 'I', not 'Heart') and its Era was wrong (Second, not Third); ZIN's Center now composes the Word GI directly rather than the raw 'dot' primitive, since GI is a Primitive only in that one context and otherwise a Word in its own right. Also fixed a real bug in both the viewer and the Glyph designer: loading a single bare primitive/word object (rather than a full file) crashed with 'Cannot read properties of undefined' — both tools now accept a full file, a single object, or an array of objects.

2026-08-20, later — Per creator: in the First Era, 'I' existed only as GI, a full Word and nothing else; the Second Era is when GI additionally gains a function as a Primitive, at the exact moment the Crystal Beings connect it to the wider position-grid pattern (ZIN/ZON) — confirming 'GI is a Primitive within ZIN, but otherwise a Word' is in-world canon, not just a schema convenience. LANGUAGE renamed to WIMBIS (its own settled sound; nothing else referenced the old id) and rebuilt again — six chevrons, WIM's diamond centered, flanked left and right by two matching small+big chevron pairs rather than one BIS split unevenly in half. Added a Word editor to the Glyph designer (compose from existing Primitives/Words, adjust position/scale/rotation, live preview, manual JSON edit, save); fixed a bug where a newly-saved Primitive didn't show up as an option for composing into a Word until an unrelated reload; replaced the original text-plus-autocomplete 'add component' field with a real dropdown after it proved unreliable for finding existing entries.

2026-08-20, even later — BIS rebuilt again, per creator: two side-by-side mirrored columns (each a big-upright/small-inverted chevron pair), not one stacked pair down the center — this is the exact motif WIMBIS echoes twice, flanking WIM, so WIMBIS turns out to reuse BIS's whole shape twice rather than splitting it in half. New Primitive 'GI' added ('Soul', role marker) — deliberately shares its id with the Word GI. Its render was defined with type 'path' on a degenerate zero-length d string, which renders as a small square (square linecap) rather than a circle; fixed to type 'dots', matching the existing 'dot' primitive. Added WIMZIN ('Perfected Language') — WIMBIS's own glyph with the (now-fixed) Primitive GI added beneath it, oversized; the visual-patch 'dot' creator had stacked on top to hide the square-rendering bug was removed since it's no longer needed.

2026-08-21 — Schema rename, per creator: the top-level 'words' array is now 'glyphs', and composition entries reference 'glyph' instead of 'word' — carried through the JSON, all three tools' code, and their UI labels, since the old terms had already caused real confusion more than once. 'dot' primitive deleted as a pure duplicate of the 'GI' primitive (identical geometry) — every former reference to 'dot' (GI-the-Glyph's own composition, GeKA, GeKARAP) now points at 'GI' instead, confirmed visually unchanged. 'teepee' deleted outright — already unused since BIS's 2026-08-19 rebuild. Both 'dot' and 'GI' had role 'marker', which is why they were showing up in the Arranger's Lines picker; corrected to 'lexical-base' (fixed 2026-08-20 for 'dot' before its deletion, same day for 'GI'). WIMZIN's Primitive-GI scale changed from 1.4 to 0.3, per creator. Glyph Designer: Primitives with render type 'rect' are now point-editable (converted to a 4-corner closed path on load — loses the distinct rect type and any corner radius, harmless today since every rect here has rx 0); 'dots'/'line-with-dot' types remain genuinely unsupported since they aren't point-sequences, now explained clearly in the tooltip instead of a generic 'not editable' note. The Designer's primitive-creation button was confusingly named 'New Glyph' even though it starts a new Primitive draft, not a Glyph — renamed to 'New Primitive' to stop colliding with the new terminology. "Open file for direct editing" is now visually the primary/recommended action (styled distinctly) with "Choose File" demoted to a clearly-labeled fallback, after creator used Choose File out of habit and got a downloaded copy instead of the in-place save they expected.

2026-08-21, later — Glyph Designer: every placed point (including ones loaded from an existing Primitive, not just freshly drawn ones) is now a real dot you can drag to move or double-click to remove, tied directly to its position in the underlying path data — verified against rect-container specifically. Category dropdown narrowed to glyph/diglyph/triglyph/tetglyph (tetglyph added for WIMZIN); a Glyph whose stored category doesn't match any of the four now shows as a clearly-labeled '(legacy)' option instead of silently snapping to the first one on save. New 'era' field added alongside category — First Era / Second Era / Third Era — with the same legacy-preserving behavior. All 19 existing Glyphs assigned both fields per creator: Glyphs — KROW, KRO, GOM, GO, GI, ZON, MO, OR; Diglyphs — KUL, OG, KULKROW, WIM, BIS, GOMGOM, GeKA, ZIN; Triglyphs — WIMBIS, GeKARAP; Tetglyph — WIMZIN (the meta-term for a 4-Glyph compound is 'GeKARI', not yet built as its own entry). First Era — everything except ZON, ZIN, WIMZIN, which are Second Era. MO and OR both settled as Glyphs despite MO's composition using two Primitives — per creator, a symmetry choice, not two combined concepts, 'admittedly deceiving' next to GOMGOM which genuinely is a Diglyph. New Primitive 'num_sign' added (the '#' shape, four crossing lines) for OR's composition. MO's composition set to two jagged-circles, rotated 90/-90 so their horns face inward and interlock in the gap between them — verified the horn-pairs actually converge toward center, not just that two circles render.

2026-08-21, later still — Added 'gom-circle', creator-hand-drawn via the Designer's new drag/remove point editing (a single continuous closed path, horns built into the circle's own outline rather than separate multipath spikes) — added alongside 'jagged-circle', not replacing it; nothing's been rewired to use it yet. Added GeKARI (spelling corrected from an initial 'GeKARAI' typo) — the Tetglyph meta-word, same construction as GI/GeKA/GeKARAP, all four outer positions filled since a Tetglyph doesn't leave one empty the way a Triglyph does. Era 'Second Era' inferred from creator's own earlier framing that Tetglyphs are a Second Era invention.

2026-08-19 — Added 6 new Lines to the Arranger, per creator, for use in an exercise: follow-1-line, follow-2-line, follow-3-line (number above the line) and goto-1-line, goto-2-line, goto-3-line (number below), all role "marker" so they show up in the Lines picker alongside ownership-line and next-idea-line. New render type "line-with-number" ({d, number, numberPosition}) added to support them, wired into all three tools' rendering code (Viewer, Arranger, Designer). A number above a Line means "follow the Expression at that position in the row (1st/2nd/3rd)"; a number below means "go to the Expression at that position" — intended to read as a forward link vs. a jump/reference, though nothing enforces that meaning yet, it's just the visual convention. A 7th Line was requested but not described — only these 6 were built; asked creator what the 7th should be rather than guessing. Also added a "Show Composition" button to the Arranger, dumping all 9 Expressions' slot contents as plain text (Line/Glyph per slot, or "(empty)") so the overall flow across Expressions can be read at a glance — deliberately unstyled per creator's "doesn't need to be pretty" instruction.

2026-08-19, later — Integrated 4 items from a hand-edited Downloads-folder copy of the file, per creator: new Primitives 'separate' (three-piece broken vertical line — two point-dots at top/bottom, disconnected from a short middle segment) and 'connect' (one unbroken vertical line); new Glyphs BE (Cut/Separate/Sever) and KA (Fix/Assemble/Maintain), both First Era. Found and fixed a bug in the source file before integrating: BE's composition referenced 'connect' instead of 'separate' — both BE and KA pointed at the same primitive, identical geometry, despite 'separate' and 'connect's own descriptions ("for BE" / "for KA") saying otherwise. Corrected BE to use 'separate', matching its own semantics and the primitive's stated purpose; flagged to creator rather than assumed silently. Also added 3 more Lines to the Arranger, filling out the set from the same conversation: wildcard-above-line and wildcard-below-line (same follow/goto meaning as the numbered Lines, but for ANY Expression in the row rather than a specific 1st/2nd/3rd — number placeholder is 0 for now), and yield-line (a line with an X through its center, representing Yield). New render type 'line-with-x' ({d, x: {cx, cy, size}}) added to support the latter, wired into all three tools' rendering code alongside 'line-with-number'.

2026-08-19, later still — Added a 'Yield Results' row to the Arranger: 3 bare Glyph slots (no Lines) below the 3x3 Expression grid, one per column, with a faint accent-colored glow — representing the Glyph a yield-line in that column resolves to. Click-to-open-menu works the same as the Expression grid's slots; Show Composition's text dump now ends with a 'Yield Results' section listing whichever of the 3 columns are filled. No JSON schema changes — this is purely Arranger UI state, not persisted data.

2026-08-19, evening — First full worked Composition written in the Arranger, per creator, using an earlier draft (all-KROW throughout) then a revised, better version (Row 1 changed from KROW to KRO) — transcribed here since the Arranger itself doesn't persist grid state to this file. Final version: Row 1 (Expr 1-3) = GOM+OG+KRO / GOM+WIM+KRO / GOM+KA+KRO, each next-idea-line-led and goto-2-line-out. Row 2 (Expr 5 only, columns 1 and 3 deliberately empty) = GOM+GI+KROW, wildcard-above-line in and wildcard-below-line out — a single mandatory gate all three Row 1 columns funnel into. Row 3 (Expr 7-9) = GOM+MO+KROW / KULKROW+KUL+KROW / GOM+OR+KROW, each follow-2-line-in and yield-line-out — note Expr 8's subject is KULKROW, not GOM, the only column where the actor changes. Yield Results: KROW, KRO, KROW. Creator-confirmed as deliberate: the KULKROW-as-subject swap on the Kill branch, and the Row-1 KROW-to-KRO change specifically 'to drive the point.' Reading (Claude's interpretation, offered and not corrected by creator beyond a timing correction on how long ago the underlying words were written): none of Gom's three verbs on Life — Create, Teach, Maintain — complete the vessel on their own; every Row 1 branch stays KRO. Completion to KROW happens exactly at GI, the Word, the language's own name for its smallest unit — the single gate every branch must pass through regardless of origin. Take and Give both preserve that completion. Kill, specifically performed by Kulkrow rather than Gom, is the one branch that reverses it, returning the vessel to its pre-Word state rather than destroying it outright. See gomsdu-codex.md's new 'Language as the Animating Gate' section and dialogue-system.md's corresponding dated entry for the cosmological and mechanical write-ups this produced.

2026-08-19, night — Session wrap-up, several smaller items from conversation rather than JSON edits: (1) GI carries a First Era reading of 'Is', alongside its established 'a Word' meaning — per creator, chevrons were the preferred grammatical tool in the First Era specifically because the whole point was directing action/intent, and 'Gom Takes/Gives Is' (the Take/Give Composition documented above) is plausibly the foundational sentence-pattern the Living Stone's entire First Era thinking runs on. (2) The Living Stone can act and 'think' via Gom's engravings but cannot originate direction, only receive it — mirrors this system's own follow-line/goto-line distinction (receiving a direction that already exists above you, versus dispatching toward one) more precisely than coincidence would explain. (3) Second Era 'gets carried away with GeKARI' per creator — the elaborate GeKA/GeKARAP/GeKARI compounding is Crystal Being overreach on top of the First Era's minimal Take/Give-Is grammar, not a necessary expansion. (4) ZINKARI (Self/ZIN at center, surrounded by GeKARI, the Tetraglyph) is confirmed as the in-world Glyph for the Player-plus-4-Character Party structure — 5 total per Party, which has independently been the settled game design for about two weeks; see gomsdu-codex.md's new 'Party Structure' section under Character Stats & Combat System. (5) The 'compass-copy' primitive shown in chat as a demo of ZINKARI's shape was never added to this file and isn't meant to be — creator plans to draw the real Glyph properly in the Designer directly. (6) Dev-facing system names (Party/Mini-Party/Meta-Party) are deliberately kept separate from World/Wimbis vocabulary (ZINKARI, GeKARI) per creator — don't blend the two even where a Wimbis word would fit the Dev concept neatly.

primitives.description: A rectangle outline with sharp, unrounded corners. Base container for the Life family of words (KROW, KRO, KULKROW).

A circle built from many short straight segments — Gom can only draw straight lines, so a circle is just a lot of them — with two small jagged horns near the top, a tiny nod to the Taurus symbol, sized small relative to the circle itself. Base container for the Gom family of words (GOM, GO).
primitives.status: redesigned 2026-08-19 — was a 12-point spiky path reading as a hexagon/star; now a 16-sided straight-edged polygon with small horns, per creator correction

primitives.description: A single angular peak, open at its base. Rotation 0deg = upright = 'W' sound / presence-marker. Rotation 180deg = inverted = 'M' sound / presence-marker. Reused rotated 90/270deg as arrowhead tips on the KUL and OG cross-words, and paired (0deg + 180deg overlapping, same position) to form a diamond — WIM is one such diamond; BIS stacks two of them at different scales. This single component does several distinct grammatical jobs depending on context, rotation, and scale — see grammar.rules.
A plain plus-sign: two perpendicular lines. Base for KUL and OG. Whichever axis carries chevron arrowheads (see those words) is the 'active' axis; the other stays a plain, unmodified line.
Original glyph for OR (Give). Creator has scrapped this design; redesign pending. Kept as a placeholder entry so the word's sound/meaning/derivation stay recorded independent of its visual form.
Original glyph for MO (Take). Creator has scrapped this design; redesign pending.
A single horizontal line. Grammatical marker indicating hierarchy and suggesting/claiming ownership between the Glyph above it and the Glyph below it in a vertical stack.

A horizontal line with a dot at its center. Grammatical marker separating one idea/clause from the next within a stacked sequence — distinct from ownership-line, which reads as possession rather than sequence.

A rhombus outline connecting the four outer positions available to a Diglyph or Triglyph's own component dots — Top, Right, Bottom, Left — leaving the fifth position, Center, open inside it. Named separately from BIS's own similarly-shaped 'diamond' (two overlapping chevrons) since this is a different construction — one single closed outline, not two chevrons meeting at a point.

"Soul" — a Primitive, creator-authored 2026-08-20, deliberately sharing an id with the Glyph GI ('a Word/single Glyph'). Fixed 2026-08-20: was defined with render type 'path' on a degenerate zero-length d string, which renders as a small square (square linecap on a zero-length path) rather than a real circle — corrected to type 'dots'. Role corrected from 'marker' to 'lexical-base' 2026-08-21 — it isn't a grammatical Line. The separate 'dot' Primitive it was originally matching against was deleted 2026-08-21 as a duplicate (identical geometry) — every former 'dot' reference (GI-the-Glyph's own composition, GeKA, GeKARAP) now points at this Primitive instead.
For OR — the '#' shape, two verticals crossing two horizontals.
Goms Circle

glyphs.etymology: ZON's exact outline, plus its Center filled with GI — the same completion-marks-presence grammar as KRO/KROW and GO/GOM, now applied to Self itself. Second Era, not Third: most people at this point were Mud People (Gom's own creations, mirroring Kulkrow's Molten Ones), and most Mud People did not have a Heart. ZIN and ZON were introduced as a deliberately unifying act — teaching everyone, Mud People included, that they had more self-awareness than previously assumed, shaped by whatever that era's Writing System and its limited Speech could actually carry.
glyphs.notes: The Crystal Beings knew exactly what Wimsib (Language — the same LANGUAGE Glyph, its BIS-half simply read in reverse, grammatically identical per the horizontal-mirroring rule) had already done to the First Era's people: reprogrammed the Living Stone's own self-understanding, replacing GOMGOM with GO|KROW. By formally claiming GI and ZON within the Language itself, they were trying to make that same erasure impossible to repeat on the Mud People. But the public meaning — 'I,' teaching universal self-awareness — carries a second, secret one underneath it: 'Heart,' reserved for the only beings who actually have one. Crystal Beings' Hearts are Rainbow Slivers. A defensive act against Gom's own playbook, and — per creator — 'basically a form of Elitism,' at the same time.

grammar.readingOrder: Vertical, top to bottom. A 'sentence' is a stack of Glyphs read downward. Horizontal placement and left-right mirroring within a single Glyph or compound carry no grammatical meaning — see 'Horizontal mirroring' below.

rules.name: Chevron completion (presence/orientation)
rules.description: A chevron attached to a base container completes the word and marks full presence/animation of what that container represents. Upright (peak up) = W-completion. Inverted (peak down) = M-completion. Absence of the chevron marks an incomplete, aura-only, unanimated form of the same base — KRO vs KROW, GO vs GOM. The completing chevron's meeting point (its apex) sits outside the container's own boundary, not inside it — crowning it from without.

rules.name: Axis rotation on the cross-shape
rules.description: The KUL/OG cross carries chevron-arrowheads on only one of its two axes; the other stays a plain line. Horizontal-active = Kill/Destroy (flanked from both sides). Vertical-active = Birth/Create (one thing above another). KUL and OG are the same base shape related by a 90-degree rotation of which axis is active — paralleling the 180-degree chevron-rotation relationship between GOM/KROW and GO/KRO.

rules.name: Slot composition / containment
rules.description: A base container's completion-slot (where its chevron would normally sit) can instead hold a different glyph entirely, changing the meaning of the whole compound. Example: KULKROW places the KUL cross in KROW's chevron-slot — a life-vessel with killing where life should be.

rules.name: Word order as direction
rules.description: Sequence alone can encode who is agent versus recipient — this is a general property of every Word in the language, not a special trick belonging to any one of them. A Word's own meaning may separately name a fixed relational direction on top of that (WIM's Teach/Learn, for instance, always runs teacher-to-pupil specifically) — that's a distinct, more advanced layer, not the same mechanism as word-order. Deferred past 1st Era Language for now.

rules.name: Position-2-3 reversal derivation
rules.description: A small, closed class of derived words are formed by taking a root word's 2nd and 3rd letters and reversing their order. KROW's letters 2-3 (R, O) reversed give OR (Give). GOM's letters 2-3 (O, M) reversed give MO (Take). The only confirmed morphological derivation process in the language so far — root-and-pattern-like, similar to how Semitic languages build words from consonant roots.

rules.name: Unmarked juxtaposition (tentative)
rules.description: It's unclear whether two Glyphs can be stacked with no marker between them and still be grammatically valid. GOMGOM (unmarked, symmetrical, interlocking) is explicitly the forbidden construction, replaced by GO|KROW (marked, hierarchical). This may mean unmarked juxtaposition is ungrammatical by design, not just culturally taboo — see openThreads.

rules.name: Horizontal mirroring carries no grammatical meaning
rules.description: Left-right placement and left-right mirroring are purely spatial/compositional choices, never grammar. A word's sound may itself be read either direction — BIS is equally valid as SIB — and a compound like LANGUAGE can flank its center element with the two halves of another word in either left-right arrangement without changing meaning. Only the vertical axis (stacking order, top-to-bottom) carries grammatical direction. Structurally neutral is not the same as culturally neutral, per creator: reading direction is a real dialect marker in-world (Humans read right-to-left, Orks left-to-right), and Sibmiw — Wimbis's own name read straight backward — is a known derogatory usage, not a harmless variant. See gomsdu-codex.md's 'A Cultural Footnote: Reading Direction.'
